newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine union chief says "ashamed" of gov't.
newsitem.headline: Argentine union chief says "ashamed" of gov't.

text.p: The head of Argentina's main union federation, the CGT, said Tuesday he was "ashamed" of the government for damaging labor relations and predicted success for Thursday's general strike.

Referring to President Carlos Menem's decrees last week to make labor markets more flexible, CGT head Rodolfo Daer told local radio he was ashamed of the administration for "destroying by decree relations between workers and employers which have 40 years of history."
The decrees signed by Menem late Wednesday came after weeks of talks with the CGT, which traditionally has close links with the governing Peronist Party, ended in stalemate.
Branding the decrees an assault on workers' rights, the CGT decided Friday to stage its third general strike this year.
Menem dismissed the strike called for Thursday, a day on which many Argentines would not work anyway, as meaningless.

The moves allow workers to decide which union health plan they sign up to and permit smaller firms to bypass national unions in collective wage talks with workers. Also, employers will now be able to appeal to the government if they want to negotiate with unions on a company-by-company and not an industry-wide basis.
The government, which plans more labor decrees, hopes that a more flexible employment market will help reduce the country's 17.3-percent joblessness rate.
